findings.description: The Mission Creek Park Pavilion, a cafe space with floor-to-ceiling windows built on the shore of Mission Creek by the developers of Mission Bay, opened for business on 1 August 2026 as the first San Francisco location of Zocalo Coffee. It had stood empty since it was finished. The building was one of the earliest structures built under the 1998 Mission Bay redevelopment plan of the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency; per city building inspection records cited by the paper it was formalised in 2001, licensed for food and beverage handling in 2002, and issued a certificate of completion in 2003. It was used as storage by the Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure, then lent free to community groups by the park's management company, and became a rental-only space when the Office transferred the Mission Bay open spaces to the Recreation and Parks Department early under the 2023 Mission Bay Parks Agreement. Rec and Park's own figures put its use at roughly three bookings a month. The neighbours who pressed for the change are named in the story and are not recorded here.

extra.redevelopment_plan: Mission Bay, finalized 1998, San Francisco Redevelopment Agency
extra.transferred_to: San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department

citation.label: Mission Local, “22 years after it was built, a cafe on the shore of Mission Creek finally opens,” 5 September 2026
citation.locator: opening paragraphs and “Empty from the early 2000s on”

raw.text: More than two decades ago, the developers building out Mission Bay constructed an elegant cafe space with floor-to-ceiling windows at 290 Channel St., on the shores of Mission Creek. On Aug. 1, 2026, it finally opened for business.

resolution.method: No record in sf-eas-addresses for 290 CHANNEL ST.
resolution.note: The address does not exist today, so there is no page it can go on. EAS has no address near it on this street either. Per "The evidence bar" in research/AGENTS.md this is a street-hub fact: a dated record of a building at a number the city no longer has.

publish.note: Blocked: the address does not exist in EAS, so there is no parcel and no page. sf-eas-addresses carries 13 Channel Street addresses and 290 is not among them — the Mission Creek Park Pavilion is a park building whose street number the city's address system does not hold. REFERENCE.md's directory rules forbid creating a page for an address that is not in EAS, and the site has no Channel Street hub either. The finding stands as a dated, sourced fact with nowhere legitimate to go; if the pavilion is ever given an EAS address, or the site settles how it documents buildings inside parks, this is ready to publish.

findings.description: Bruno's, the nightclub at 20th and Mission that closed in the first days of the Covid-19 pandemic, announced it would reopen with a soft opening on 12 September 2026, six years after it went dark, with test-run events each weekend in September and a possible grand opening in the first week of October. The story records that the business has occupied 2389 Mission Street for more than sixty years and was formerly an Italian restaurant and a labour hangout. A 2023 reopening was delayed over city permits; the Board of Supervisors backed a new liquor licence in February 2024. The current and former owners and the general manager are named in the story and are not recorded here, as none is an architect, builder, developer or firm.

extra.occupancy_reported: more than 60 years at this address

citation.label: Mission Local, “Bruno’s nightclub set to re-open next week after 6 year closure,” 4 September 2026

raw.text: It’s been a long wait for a business that has occupied 2389 Mission St for over 60 years.

findings.description: Mission Local's report that the mayor would indefinitely continue a '90 day strategy' of ambassadors and activations on the Mission BART plazas named two street addresses, both of them the businesses of merchants the reporter interviewed about whether the plazas felt better. Neither address is the subject of the story and nothing is established about either building.

publish.note: Both addresses are passing mentions — the storefronts of quoted business owners. The story is about a policy on two BART plazas, and it establishes nothing about either building. It fails the ten-year test.
